provision: A record dated in a month already settled early is paid as a (YYYY-MM) line of the next period. EPF (all three schedules), SOCSO, EIS and SKBBK bill it as a top-up of its earned month's bill, under that month's version; PCB and the HRD Corp levy bill it with the month it is paid.
citation: EPF Act 1991 (Act 452) s.43(1) and Third Schedule (contribution on the amount of wages for the month); Employees' Social Security Act 1969 (Act 4) s.6 and Third Schedule (wages for the month), which also schedules SKBBK on Act 4 s.2(24) wages; Employment Insurance System Act 2017 (Act 800) s.18 and Second Schedule (wages for the month); Income Tax (Deduction from Remuneration) Rules 1994 r.3 with the LHDN MTD 2026 specification (remuneration is deducted in the month it is paid); Act 612 ss.2, 14 (monthly wages include arrears).
reason: Gated by tests/payroll-run-orderings.test.ts, the 'leave and overtime recorded after the early settlement' and 'an off-cycle bonus after the next period's late lines' cases at a low, middle and high wage: each late line is paid once; an EARNED scheme's two months and year to date equal the combined path to the cent, a later run of the paid month billing the late lines and their top-up as the earned month's (`payslips.adjustments.earned_period`, `payslips.statutory.earned_*`); a PAID scheme's late statutory equals bill(next month incl. the late lines) − bill(next month without them). The named goldens are built so each EARNED scheme's late lines cross a band edge, rate band or ceiling differently in the two months, and assert that billing it PAID would move its figures. Unset is PAID, a lawful cash-basis default. EPF, SOCSO, EIS and SKBBK: the Acts price the wages for the month, so a late line is wages of the month it was earned. PCB: MTD treats remuneration in the month paid (owner decision 2026-10-01). HRDF: Act 612 s.2 counts arrears inside a month's wages, so the levy reads a late line in the month it is paid.
